title: docs(spec): V3_MIGRATION_GUIDE announced a relocation that never happened, and the census gains a standing unpublished-subpath control
body:
Fixes #18753

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Two halves, both required by the dispatch: (A) make the document true, and (B) turn this card into a fixture the census instrument cannot lose when the document is repaired.

All readings below were taken in this worktree at base `62b114f8b8` (the seat's readings were taken at `be7aeb8275`, so every one was re-measured rather than inherited). Commit cited for the gate and lint runs: `8ac750cfe9`.

## What the re-measurement found, and where it departs from the dispatch

The card framed one fork: repoint the specifier, or declare the subpath. The dispatching seat had already shown route (1) and route (2) are both unavailable for two of the three. Re-measuring confirmed that and added the cause:

| Claim in the guide | Measured at `62b114f8b8` |
|---|---|
| helpers "moved to `@objectstack/core/errors`" / `@objectstack/core/plugin` | **False.** `466f32ea22` ("v3.0: Remove all deprecated items") **deleted** them: 25 removed lines naming the three symbols, **0 added** lines naming them. It created neither destination. |
| the three symbols exist somewhere | **No.** Zero `.ts`/`.tsx` files repo-wide name `createErrorResponse`, `getHttpStatusForCategory` or `definePlugin`. Bright control on the same `git grep`: `defineStack` reads **368** files. |
| `@objectstack/core` serves those subpaths | **No.** Its `exports` map has exactly two entries, `.` and `./logger`. |
| "`ErrorResponseSchema`, `PluginDefinitionSchema` etc. remain in `@objectstack/spec`" | **Half false.** `ErrorResponseSchema (const)` is at `api-surface/api.json:364`; `PluginDefinitionSchema` reads **0** across every `api-surface/*.json` file. |

The guide was created `2026-02-11`; the removal landed `2026-02-12`. It predicted a relocation one day before a commit that did not perform it, and ticked the checklist anyway. So the defect is not three unresolvable imports — it is **a false completion declaration**, and there is no resolving specifier to substitute because nothing was ever published to replace these.

### Departure: line 28 keeps `@objectstack/spec/hub`, deliberately

The dispatch prescribed repointing line 28 at `@objectstack/spec/system`. **This PR does not do that**, on the dispatch's own single criterion — *after the repair, every sentence the document says must be true of this tree today*.

Line 28 sits inside a block headed `// ❌ v2.x (deprecated, removed in v3.0)`, and the ✅ block directly beneath it already says `import { TenantSchema } from '@objectstack/spec/system';`. Repointing line 28 would make the ❌ and ✅ blocks identical and have the guide assert that the **current, supported** import is the one v3.0 removed. That is a worse falsehood than the one being repaired, and it deletes the document's only statement of what to migrate *away from*.

Two measurements make the case stronger than a style preference:

1. **Line 28 contributes nothing to the census number anyway.** Its block reports `TS1109` only — a syntax error from `parse({ ... })` — so it lands in pass 1's unparseable set and tsc never type-checks it. `@objectstack/spec/hub` produces **no TS2307 at all** in the corpus today. The card's "measured as TS2307" holds for two of the three specifiers, not three.
2. Both remaining ❌ blocks (sections 2 and 4) have the same property: they are true depictions of removed APIs. The instrument's own docblock already concedes this category for `CHANGELOG.md` — "before/after migration snippets that deliberately show removed APIs. A failing block here is frequently CORRECT documentation."

What the ❌ blocks did get is an explicit in-block disclaimer, modelled on the shape `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx` already uses in this repository (a warn callout naming what does not exist, repeated as an in-block comment at the point of use): each now says it is shown so you can find and delete it, and must not be copied.

⇒ If the seat prefers the prescription as written, or prefers de-fencing the ❌ blocks into prose so they leave the TypeScript population entirely, both are one-line follow-ups. They are recorded as open questions rather than taken unilaterally.

## (A) What changed in the document

- Section 2 renamed "Runtime Logic Extraction" to "Runtime Helper Removal" — no inbound anchor references it — and now states the removal with **no destination**, above a callout naming the relocation that never happened.
- The table's "New Location" column is now "v3.0 disposition", reading "Removed — no replacement export" on all three rows.
- The ✅ code block is gone. There is no ✅ counterpart to paste. In its place: prose pointing at what actually exists — `ErrorResponseSchema` still describes the envelope, and a plugin is an ordinary object or class matching the `Plugin` interface exported from `@objectstack/core` via `export * from './types.js'`.
- The two checklist items are **unticked** and reworded. The tick was the false claim; unticking it is the first half of the repair, the wording the second.
- The note drops `PluginDefinitionSchema` and names it as exported from no entrypoint.

⛔ Nothing was pointed at `packages/runtime/src/error-envelope.ts` (`buildApiError` / `apiErrorResponse`), although it is the closest live thing: it is **not** re-exported from `@objectstack/runtime`'s index, so naming it would repeat exactly the defect this card is about.

## (B) The synthetic control leg

`UNPUBLISHED_SUBPATH_CONTROL` reconstructs the three specifiers line for line as the guide carried them before this repair, alongside a frozen `UNPUBLISHED_SUBPATH_SPECIFIERS` roster the block is held equal to by a battery.

It is synthetic for the reason `FIRING_CONTROL` is: a control that IS the live document disarms itself the moment the document is repaired, and the fourth instance in the next guide would be just as green. It carries no elision marker and no syntax error, both load-bearing — a marker would let the disqualified exclusion reading skip it, and a syntax error would put it in pass 1's unparseable set where the three TS2307s it exists to produce are never reported. That second point is not theoretical: it is precisely what hides line 28 from the corpus, so **the synthetic leg measures a specifier the live document never did.**

### The refusal-list question, and its cost

**Decision: the leg joins `controlProblems()`.** When it misbehaves, the whole census refuses.

- What it guards is the **tolerance rule**, not the corpus. Widen `classifyDiagnostic` until an `@objectstack/*` TS2307 is forgiven and every unresolvable documented import in the repository goes quiet at once. `FIRING_CONTROL` is a TS2341 and cannot notice; before this PR the census had **no** standing control for the `unpublished-subpath` family — the family this card is an instance of.
- Self-test-only was the alternative, and it leaves that hole open: the census would keep printing numbers nobody could trust.
- **The cost, stated plainly:** if one of the three subpaths is ever genuinely published, the leg stops producing TS2307 for it and **every census refuses** until someone edits the fixture. That is the same exposure `FIRING_CONTROL` already carries — make `ObjectKernel.logger` public and it stops producing TS2341 — and it is answered the same way: the refusal text names the remedy (repoint at a subpath still in no `exports` entry, ⛔ never delete the leg, which takes the other two guards with it) instead of leaving a stale fixture to be diagnosed.

Five batteries register against it and `SELF_TEST_BATTERY_FLOOR` rises **30 → 35**. Two of the five drive `controlProblems()` directly, and each first asserts a healthy control trio reports **zero** problems before asserting a broken one reports some — otherwise a `controlProblems` that always complained would pass.

## Evidence

**LIT — the leg fires, proven by ablation.** Each ablation asserted the tree equalled HEAD first, proved the mutation reached disk by occurrence count and changed blob hash, restored from HEAD under a trap, and proved restoration by `git diff HEAD` being empty and the blob matching `12ec6b3955b4e6fdff880705eee5a67c9b457bf6`.

| Ablation | `--self-test` | census |
|---|---|---|
| widen tolerance, `forgiven: false` to `true` on the `@objectstack/` branch | **exit 1**, 2 failures | **exit 1** — refuses, naming all three specifiers as `forgiven=true` |
| drop the five roster rows | **exit 1**, 6 failures, floor reports "declares 30 batteries, below the pinned 35" | not exercised |
| drop it from `controlUnits()` | not exercised | **exit 1** — "UNPUBLISHED_SUBPATH_CONTROL did not extract to a block" |

**DARK — nothing else moved.** `--self-test` 30 cases / 30 batteries before, **35 / 35** after, exit 0; a roster diff against the base proves **0** of the original 30 batteries were dropped. `FIRING_CONTROL` is byte-identical in behaviour across both censuses: "reports 5 diagnostic(s) including TS2341 at block line 13", elision marker still present. `GREEN_CONTROL` compiles clean in both.

**Census, before and after** (full build first — both readings share one build, so only the document differs):

|  | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `unpublished-subpath` family | `8 diagnostics in 7 blocks` | `6 diagnostics in 6 blocks` |
| this file's share of that | 2 (`@objectstack/core/errors`, `@objectstack/core/plugin`, both in the block at line 72) | **0** |
| `V3_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` | `7 blocks / 5 RAW / 5 TOLERANT` | `7 blocks / 5 RAW / 5 TOLERANT` |
| hand-written stratum | 282 blocks / 195 RAW / 76 TOLERANT | unchanged |

The dispatch expected `5 TOLERANT` to fall. **It did not, and that is the correct outcome** — measured per block rather than asserted. The repaired block went from 11 diagnostics to 3: both TS2307 gone, and all five TS2300 "duplicate identifier" gone too, since those were an artefact of the ❌ and ✅ lines importing the same names into one block. What remains is `TS2724` + `TS2305` x2 — "no exported member" against `@objectstack/spec/api` and `@objectstack/spec/kernel` — which is the block correctly reporting that it depicts symbols v3.0 removed. Every one of this file's five failing blocks is a ❌ example, and failing is what a ❌ example does.

The remaining 6 in the family are all `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` naming `@objectstack/spec/cloud` — release-owned history, out of scope here.

**Gates.** Derived with `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` from the merge base, re-derived after `git fetch origin main` and **identical**: **65 families, 65 run, 65 exit 0**, reconciled back through `--ran` with exit codes recorded (a derived zero, not a claimed one). `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` exit 0.

**Lint.** Not narrowed — the repo-wide scan fitted in budget: `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` linted **6848** files with **0** messages, exit 0, at `8ac750cfe9`. (Type-aware linting is not enabled in `eslint.config.mjs`, so the narrowing argument was available and turned out to be unnecessary.)

**Publish surface.** `V3_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` is matched by **0** `files[]` entries in any package manifest (positive control: `README.md` **is** in `@objectstack/spec`'s `files[]`), and `scripts/` belongs to the private root package. So nothing this diff touches publishes, which is the `skip-changeset` criterion, and `lint.yml` names this exact case in its own prose: "this PR edits a CI-internal script is the textbook `skip-changeset` case — such a PR releases nothing". ⚠️ The `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line above is the dispatching seat's mechanical-floor declaration, carried verbatim as instructed; it is a routing declaration, not this PR's measurement, and the measurement above reads the other way. Flagged for the seat's in-seat re-review rather than changed here.

## Acceptance notes

Observed while measuring, ⛔ not filed and ⛔ not repaired here:

- The `unpublished-subpath` family count is a **lower bound**, not a total. A syntax error anywhere in a block sends it to pass 1's unparseable set, where no semantic diagnostic is ever reported — which is exactly why line 28's `@objectstack/spec/hub` is invisible. 18 hand-written blocks are syntax-only-unforgiven and could each be masking more. The instrument documents the two-pass mechanism and calls it honest; what is not stated is that the family totals inherit a floor from it. Successor: #18715's wiring letter needs that caveat beside the number.
- `packages/spec/src/benchmark.bench.ts:120` calls `(Kernel as any).PluginDefinitionSchema.parse(validPlugin)` on a symbol exported from no entrypoint. The `as any` is what lets it compile. Successor: whoever next touches that bench.
- `packages/spec/V3_MIGRATION_GUIDE.md` is a before/after migration guide sitting in the census's `handwritten` stratum, whose contract reads "a failing block here is a defect an author can repair". For this document's ❌ blocks that is false, and after this repair all five of its remaining TOLERANT failures are correct documentation. This is a real input to #18715's wiring decision, since it is part of what a gate would be asked to hold at zero.
- The same never-performed relocation is asserted in `packages/spec/DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md:463-465`, `packages/spec/ZOD_SCHEMA_AUDIT_REPORT.md` and root `CHANGELOG.md:2289-2290`. Left untouched by the dispatch's read-only fence; the seat files these.
- The document's title, "Target Release: Q2 2026" and "Last Updated: 2026-02-11" sit against packages at version 17.4.0. Not touched: out of this card's scope, and no reader is misdirected to an unresolvable import by it.

⛔ `packages/spec/package.json` and `packages/core/package.json` were not opened for editing. Route (2) was never needed: it is impossible for two of the three specifiers, since a module that does not exist cannot be declared in an `exports` map.
